name: NavLink
description: Navigation anchor primitive used inside `SiteHeader`, `Footer`, and in-page navs. Renders an underlying `next/link` and applies the `aria-current='page'` token when the active route matches.

ariaRequirements: Sets `aria-current='page'` on the active route so the active nav item is announced.
Renders a real `<a>` (via next/link) for native browser behaviour.
a11y.reviewedNote: 2026-05-28 — Bucket-1 beta port: keyboard/ARIA contract reviewed, ForcedColors story added, Storybook axe gate (parameters.a11y.test: error).

forbiddenUse: Use inside body prose — that is `Link`.
Use as a button — primary actions belong on `Button`.
dense: Next.js nav link deriving active state from usePathname (prefix match, exact opt-in); sets aria-current=page; styled via className/activeClassName/inactiveClassName (Tailwind-token defaults by design)

usage.description: NavLink is the router-aware navigation link for site chrome: headers, drawers, and sidebars. It compares the current pathname against `href` — prefix match by default, exact with `exact` — and reflects the result both as `aria-current="page"` and as the active/inactive class pair. Use it inside a labelled `<nav>`; for inline prose links use Link instead. Styling is deliberately className-driven (Tailwind tokens by default) so each navigation surface owns its look while the active-state contract stays shared.

bestPractices.description: Wrap groups in a labelled <nav aria-label="Primary"> so assistive tech can jump to the landmark.
Use exact on short roots like "/" — prefix matching would otherwise mark Home active on every route.
Keep active styling redundant with aria-current: weight or underline plus color, never color alone.
Override className/activeClassName per surface instead of wrapping; the active-state logic is the shared part.
Do not use NavLink for inline body links — that is Link's job; NavLink's route tracking is navigation-chrome behavior.
Do not hand-set aria-current on children; the component derives it from the route.
